quotes.text: Built on remains of a Brigittine Abbey nunnery (1430-70). Part of C15 undercroft remains. Protector Somerset reconstructed the house in 1547-52, substantially in its present shape.
The house, 3-storeys with crenellated top and gable turrets, is built on a hollow square. East front ground floor loggia mid C17.

Remodelled inside and out by Robert Adam 1767-5. In 1874 the Percy Lion, transferred from Old Northumberland House at Charing Cross was erected on the river front. Slight war damage, 2nd floor of North West tower rebuilt; 2 statues on columns in anteroom destroyed.

note: Tranche 3, English Baroque / Palladian / Adam cluster, 5 Sep 2026. THE RECORD IS NAMED 'Syon House interiors' BECAUSE THE EXEMPLAR IS, AND THE JOIN KEYS MAY NOT BE RENAMED; the building is Syon House and `aka` says so. THE ENTRY DESCRIBES A JACOBETHAN SHELL AND NOT AN ADAM INTERIOR. Two extracts with different queries returned the same paragraph, and in it the twelve verd-antique columns of the Ante-Room, the apsed Long Gallery, the Great Hall and the Dining Room -- everything this node exists for -- appear only as '2 statues on columns in anteroom destroyed'. For the flagship interior scheme of British neoclassicism the National Heritage List states three storeys, a hollow square and a broken date. Historic England serves the Details section hard-wrapped. Every run of whitespace in these quotes is the extractor's line wrap collapsed to one space; nothing else was changed, and a word broken across a wrap is left broken. No rights line for the list entry TEXT was read verbatim here, so no `rights_evidence` is recorded rather than a borrowed one.
